key_insight: DreamLite shows that a unified diffusion model with only 0.39B parameters can run on-device and support both text-to-image generation and text-guided image editing with practical latency and footprint.
problem_solved: Large diffusion models (billions of parameters) are too heavy for low-latency, on-device use, and existing lightweight models mostly support only T2I generation—not editing. DreamLite closes this gap by providing a compact, unified model for both tasks.
method: Compact diffusion backbone (~0.39B params) built with parameter-efficient architectural choices to retain generative quality while reducing size.
Unified conditioning scheme that accepts text plus image reference and optional edit masks, enabling the same model to perform both T2I generation and text-guided image editing.
On-device optimizations (e.g., quantization-aware training, distillation from larger teachers, and latency-aware pruning/architecture choices) to minimize runtime and memory footprint.
impact: Enables deployment of generation + editing capabilities directly on mobile and edge devices, reducing latency, storage, and privacy risks while making advanced image workflows accessible to practitioners and product teams.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: compact diffusion U‑Net with labeled modules (shared latent, text branch, reference/mask branch) and the 0.39B parameter callout.
Before/after editing triplets: original image → edit prompt/mask → edited output to demonstrate editing fidelity.
Latency vs. model size chart: compare DreamLite to large diffusion models and prior on-device T2I models (parameters on x-axis, latency on y-axis).
Training & deployment pipeline: teacher distillation + quantization → compact model → on-device inference flow.
paper_title: DreamLite: A Lightweight On-Device Unified Model for Image Generation and Editing
paper_authors: Kailai Feng, Yuxiang Wei, Bo Chen, Yang Pan, Hu Ye
